<!-- README.md -->

# Linecaster

### Modular OCR pipelines you can run anywhere

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/linecaster.png" alt="Line drawing of an Intertype C4 linecaster, a hot-metal typesetting machine" width="353">
</p>
<p align="center"><sub>An Intertype C4 linecaster (1961), after a photograph in the Science Museum Group
Collection, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. <a href="#-license">Credit</a></sub></p>

Linecaster turns page images into text. You build an OCR pipeline from interchangeable steps (a model that
reads the text, layout, tables, formulas, post-processing) and run it unchanged on a laptop, a GPU server, a
Ray or Slurm cluster or [Hugging Face Jobs][HF Jobs].

- 🧩 **Any step is replaceable.** A vision-language model or a line recognizer reads the text; layout, table
  and formula models and rule-based post-processing are separate steps.
- 🌍 **Any machine.** Only the command line changes, never the pipeline.
- 🎯 **The same result everywhere.** A page's text depends only on that page and the pinned models.
- 🔁 **Built for long runs.** Interrupted runs resume; failed pages are set aside with the reason.
- 🏛️ **Built on standards, not on one collection.** Folders, buckets, IIIF and METS manifests, OAI-PMH; ALTO,
  PAGE-XML, hOCR, Parquet and JSON Lines out. Project-specific code belongs in projects built on it.

📖 **Docs:** [storytracer.github.io/linecaster](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/): the reference, a page
for every block and catalog entry, and [`llms.txt`](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/latest/llms.txt) for
coding agents.

## 🚀 Quick start

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 0.13.6 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
uv run launch.py                               # list the recipes and models
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium         # the modular pipeline, a preset per step
uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/   # run a vision-language model (needs vLLM and a GPU)
```

You get one page record per page in `out/pages/`. Add `--files out/files --formats md,alto` for per-page files.

> [!NOTE]
> Every pipeline is a self-contained [uv script][uv scripts] with pinned dependencies and a lock file next to it.
> `uv run` installs what it needs on the first run; models download on first use.

## 🧭 Three ways to transcribe

**1. A recipe**: a tested combination of presets, one per step, with its own edition. Each recipe has a script
of its own in `recipes/`, which brings exactly the engines it needs:

```bash
uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/
```

The same without a checkout, from the script's URL:

```bash
uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py scans/ out/
```

**2. A vision-language model** reads each page, or each layout region. It runs behind [vLLM] or [SGLang], so it
needs an NVIDIA GPU and the `vllm` command on the PATH.

```bash
uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0
```

**3. The modular pipeline**: layout, lines and a line recognizer, then post-processing. You choose a preset for
every step; `linecaster models` lists them.

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium \
  --typography ratios --recomposition unicode-recomposition --composition docling-composition
```

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--layout single-region` | the whole page as one region, no layout model |
| `--tables`, `--formulas` | add table and formula recognition |
| `--typography` | headings and their levels |
| `--recomposition` | running text in paragraphs (without it, the page stays as laid out) |
| `--composition` | the page's document, for Markdown, HTML and JSON |
| `--set recognition.batch_size=4` | change one option of a preset |
| `--files DIR --formats md,alto` | per-page files: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON |
| `--dry-run` | print the plan and its graph, run nothing |

Options after a recipe's name override single steps; the run record lists them.

## 📥 Input

| Pages from | Flags |
|---|---|
| a folder of images | `IMAGES` (`--item-from-parent`: each subfolder is an item) |
| a list of images | `IMAGES --paths-file pages.txt` |
| Parquet with an image column | `--parquet PATH` (`--image-key`, `--item-key`, `--sequence-key`) |
| IIIF or METS manifests | `--manifests FOLDER`, `--manifests list.txt`, or `--manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url` |
| an earlier run | `--pages OUT/pages` |

Any fsspec path works: local, `s3://`, `hf://`, `http(s)://`. linecaster reads IIIF Presentation and METS/MODS
manifests itself; `--existing-ocr` also keeps the library's own OCR as `ocr_original`. PDF files are read by the `PdfReader` block (extra `pypdfium2`).
`--sample 10000 --sample-per-item 8` reads a fixed sample of the input instead, chosen by hashes of its ids before
any image is read and the same whatever the setup (`OUT/sample.parquet`; `linecaster sample` without a run).

For large collections, fetch the images once, then transcribe, then bind the pages into items:

```bash
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url OUT --rate-limit 5/1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT2/pages OUT3 --recipe item-texts
```

## 📦 Output

| Output | For |
|---|---|
| 🗂️ Page records ([JSON Lines], [Parquet]) | later pipelines: every intermediate result |
| 🏛️ [ALTO], [PAGE-XML], [hOCR] | libraries and viewers: every word with its position |
| 📝 Markdown, HTML, DocLang, [Docling] JSON | documents with headings, tables and formulas |
| 📜 `verbatim_txt` per item | the text as printed, for checking against a transcription |
| 📖 `readable_txt`, `readable_md` per item | reading and training: letterforms folded, hyphens joined, paragraphs flowed |

The text as written is always kept; readable text is derived from it. All text is Unicode [NFC]; spelling is never
modernized. Rejected pages go to `rejects/` with the reason. Every run is traced with [OpenTelemetry] into
`OUT/traces/` (nothing is sent anywhere unless you set the `OTEL_*` variables), and `linecaster traces OUT` shows
where the time went.

## 🌍 Run anywhere

| Where | Flags |
|---|---|
| 💻 this machine | none: models load inside the pipeline |
| 🖥️ this machine, with a model server | `--backend served` |
| 🧮 a Ray cluster | `--on ray --tasks 64` |
| ☁️ Hugging Face Jobs | `--on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha>` |
| 🏛️ a Slurm cluster | from Python, with datatrove's `SlurmPipelineExecutor` ([below](#%EF%B8%8F-your-own-pipeline)) |

On Ray and HF Jobs every task gets one GPU and starts its own model server. A rerun into the same output folder
runs only the tasks that didn't finish.

<details>
<summary><b>A model server that stays up</b></summary>

```bash
P="--layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve $P
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1
```

A recipe's script serves its models too: `uv run launch.py squiddle serve`, then `uv run launch.py squiddle scans/
out/ --backend served --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1`.

For a vision-language model, `--recognition-endpoint` points `transcribe_vlm.py` at a running vLLM or SGLang.
Servers listen on loopback only.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Ray</b></summary>

`ray` runs Ray's own command line with the pipeline's packages, so every machine has the same versions:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --on ray --tasks 64
```

Images, output and the logging folder must be on storage every machine can reach, such as an `s3://` bucket.

Each task reserves `--cpus-per-task` CPUs (default 12), `--mem-per-cpu-gb` GiB of memory per CPU (default 4, so
48 GiB), or `--mem-per-task-gb` GiB whatever its CPUs, and one GPU. Start every worker with at least that much:
`ray start --num-cpus`, `--memory` and `--num-gpus`. Before it submits anything, a launch checks that a live node can
run a task, and stops with what a task needs and what the nodes have. It also logs how many tasks fit at once.
`--no-fit-check` leaves the check out, for a cluster that adds nodes on demand. Each task sizes its thread pools
(OpenMP, BLAS, OpenCV, torch) to its CPUs, not to the machine's.

**On Kubernetes**, one Deployment can run the head and another the workers:

- Start Ray in each pod through the pipeline script (`uv run pipelines/<script>.py ray start …`), so the pods run the
  script's locked packages.
- Give each worker pod the CPUs, memory and GPU a task reserves, plus room for `/dev/shm` (Ray's object store),
  and pass the same amounts to `ray start --num-cpus/--memory/--num-gpus`. A pod with one GPU holds one task.
- With the data on object storage the pods need only ephemeral storage: the environment, the model weights and
  Ray's temporary files.
- Submit the run to the head with `ray job submit`, so it runs inside the cluster and outlives the session that
  submitted it. A driver outside the cluster must reach every node.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Hugging Face Jobs</b></summary>

One GPU per Job; each Job installs Linecaster at a pushed commit with the pipeline's pinned dependencies.

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py s3://<bucket>/images hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/<run> $P \
  --paths-file hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/pages.txt --env FSSPEC_S3_ANON=true \
  --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --tasks 4000 --workers 64
```

`--workers` Jobs run at once. `--flavor l4x4 --gpus 4` runs four tasks per Job. `--dry-run` launches nothing.

</details>

## ✍️ Your own pipeline

A pipeline is a list of blocks; [datatrove] runs it. This is the modular pipeline, cut down:

```python
from datatrove.executor import LocalPipelineExecutor
from linecaster.backends import InProcess as P
from linecaster.blocks.composition import (
    Composer, Recomposer, Typographer)
from linecaster.blocks.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.blocks.lines import (
    LineAssigner, LineDetector)
from linecaster.blocks.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.blocks.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.blocks.text import UnicodeNormalizer
from linecaster.blocks.writers import PageFileWriter

pipeline = [
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLayoutEngine")),
    LineDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLineEngine")),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer(
        P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleRecognitionEngine")),
    UnicodeNormalizer(),
    Typographer("ratios@1"),
    Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1"),
    Composer("docling-composition@1"),
    PageFileWriter("out/", formats=("md", "alto")),
]
LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline, logging_dir="out/logs").run()
```

The same list runs on a Slurm cluster through [datatrove]'s Slurm executor: one array job, one GPU per task, in an
environment that has the engines (`venv_path`):

```python
from datatrove.executor import SlurmPipelineExecutor

SlurmPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline, tasks=64, time="04:00:00", partition="gpu",
    gpus_per_task=1, venv_path="/path/to/venv",
    logging_dir="out/logs").run()
```

Every block declares what it reads and adds, so a pipeline is checked before it starts: a recognizer without
lines fails at once, with every problem listed. Put the script in `pipelines/` with the `# /// script` block of
`pipelines/transcribe_modular.py` (it brings the engines) and build it with `linecaster.runtime.run.main` to get
the pipelines' command line on every machine. The [pipelines reference](docs/reference/pipelines.md) covers
backends, partial runs (`--until`, `--after`) and the builder.

## 🧩 How it works

1. **One record per page.** Every step reads the page's `Transcription` and adds its part: regions, lines, text,
   tables, a document. Steps share the data model and nothing else.
2. **Contracts.** Each block declares what it reads, adds, replaces or removes; the builder checks the pipeline
   and draws its graph from them.
3. **Backends.** A model step runs `InProcess`, `Served` (a model server reached through [saturate], which keeps
   the GPU busy) or `Chat` (a vision-language model behind an OpenAI-compatible server).
4. **Executors.** [datatrove] splits the pages into tasks, runs them locally, on [Ray], on Slurm or on HF Jobs, and
   resumes where a run stopped.

Models batch only the lines of one page, and model revisions and numerically relevant libraries are pinned, so
a page's output never depends on the machine or on what else runs. Different GPU types can still differ in rare
single characters.

## 🧰 Models and blocks

Every configuration is a **preset** in Linecaster's catalog: an engine, a model at a pinned revision with its
original model card, and settings. Released editions never change. Vision-language models run behind vLLM or
SGLang; the other models run inside the pipeline or behind `linecaster serve`, one package per engine:
`linecaster-kraken` ([kraken]), `linecaster-paddlex` ([PaddleX]) and `linecaster-tesseract` ([Tesseract]).

Every preset and recipe, with its model and settings: [the catalog](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/latest/catalog/).

Every block by family, with its contract, backends and options: [the blocks](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/latest/blocks/).

## 🏷️ Versions

The current release is `v0.5.4`; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists each release's changes, upgrade notes first.
While the version is 0.x, a breaking release raises the minor version (0.3 → 0.4) and every other release the patch
version ([versions and releases](docs/reference/compatibility.md#versions-and-releases)); there are no deprecation
periods yet. The
[docs site](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/) keeps a version per release, `latest` for the newest.
For `main`, run `uv run linecaster docs` and then `uv run --group docs mkdocs serve` in a checkout.

<!-- docs/reference/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

The terms linecaster uses, one meaning each. Where a word means something else elsewhere (in datatrove, Haystack,
everyday use), the **not** column says so. Code, docs and commit messages use these terms and no others; a new
term is added here before it is used.

## Running things

| Term | Meaning | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **block** | One processing unit of a pipeline: a datatrove `PipelineStep`. Blocks are named as role nouns (`LineRecognizer`, `Composer`, `PageJsonlWriter`). An HTTP server's refusal is a *block* too, always named with its host or proxy (below, **block (HTTP)**). | not a "step" (that is a catalog term), not a "component", not a "module" |
| **role** | What a block does, defined by its contract; implementations and strategies of one role are interchangeable. | |
| **family** | A group of roles of one kind: readers, layout, lines, recognition, conversion, text, composition, binding, validation, servers, writers, composites. One subpackage of `linecaster.blocks` each. | |
| **contract** | What a block reads, adds, replaces and removes in the page record (or item record), and its unit. The builder checks contracts before a run. | not a Python type signature |
| **part** | One named piece of the page record (or item record) a contract names: page-level (`image`, `metadata`), or of one transcription (`ocr_new:lines`); the vocabulary is `PARTS` (below). | not a datatrove `Document` field |
| **unit** | What one call of a block or engine processes: `line`, `region`, `page` or `item`. | |
| **per-unit transform**, **stream transform** | The two shapes of a block: a per-unit transform processes one unit per call and its base class owns the loop; a stream transform takes the whole stream and passes each unit on when it is done, possibly out of order (served model blocks). | |
| **condition** | A picklable predicate on the page record with a `describe()`; a block with one (`when=`) processes only the pages it accepts, the others pass unchanged. Blocks sharing a group are **alternatives**: each page goes through one of them. | |
| **composite block** | A named group of blocks with its own outward contract (e.g. `ModularTranscriber`). The builder expands it into its blocks. | |
| **pipeline** | An ordered list of blocks that a stream of pages (or items) passes through, run by an executor. datatrove's sense. | not a graph of components as in Haystack |
| **graph** | The dependencies between a pipeline's blocks, derived from their contracts by the builder: for checking, drawing, and cutting into stages. It is not executed as a graph. | |
| **builder** | The code that turns a pipeline definition into stages: derives the graph, checks it, expands composites, cuts it at unit changes. | |
| **stage** | One datatrove pipeline run as part of a longer computation; stages run one after another and hand over through files (e.g. page records written in item shards, read by the next stage). | not a "phase" |
| **pipeline shape** | One way of putting blocks together, with slots for presets: the code in `linecaster.pipelines.<name>` that adds its options, names the engines they ask for and builds its blocks, with its help text, pipeline id and slots. Named like its pipeline script and its pipeline id; a derivative's script imports it the same way. | not the blocks of one run (that is the pipeline) |
| **pipeline script** | A self-contained uv script in `pipelines/` (PEP 723 metadata, a lock next to it) that gives one pipeline shape its environment and its command line, and runs it on every executor. Named as a verb: `harvest.py`, `transcribe_modular.py`, `transcribe_vlm.py`, `bind.py`. | |
| **pipeline id** | A pipeline script's versioned id, its file name plus `.v<n>`: `transcribe_modular.v1`. Recipes name the pipeline they run by it. | |
| **workflow** | The sequence of pipeline scripts for a collection: harvest → transcribe → bind. | not one pipeline; not a GitHub Actions workflow (say "CI workflow" for that) |
| **executor**, **job**, **task**, **worker**, **shard** | datatrove's terms: the executor runs a pipeline as tasks; a job is one launch (one HF Job, one Slurm job); a task is one unit of work with its own rank; workers are tasks running at once; a shard is the part of the input one task reads. | |
| **item shard** | A folder of page records holding every page of a set of items, so that a later stage reads whole items. | not a datatrove shard |
| **backend** | Where a model block's engine runs: `in-process`, `served` (a server reached through saturate), or `chat` (an OpenAI-compatible VLM server). | not the executor |
| **server** | A process that hosts models: `linecaster serve` for engines, vLLM or SGLang for VLMs, a service for a page engine. Started by the server blocks `ModelServer`, `ChatModelServer` and `ServiceServer`, which go last in a pipeline. | |
| **service** | The server a page engine talks to that is neither `linecaster serve` nor a chat server: a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API, in the vendor's image (Falcon-OCR, OXR-1.0), or the vLLM a vendor's package attaches to (surya-ocr). A page preset's `serve` block names it; `ServiceServer` starts it. | not an operating-system service |
| **observer** | A callback at block boundaries (before and after a unit): taps, sampling, progress, tracing. | not a Haystack "hook" |
| **boundary step** | The step the builder puts after a block when a stage has observers: it tells them that each unit left that block and entered the next. It adds no stats. | not a block |
| **tap** | An observer that writes the page records as they pass a given block (`--tap-after`). | |
| **partial run** | A run of part of a pipeline: up to a block (`--until`), or from page records after one (`--after`). | |
| **run folder** | The output folder of a run (`OUT`): `pages/` (the page records), `rejects/`, `logs/`, `traces/`, `run.yaml`, with a sample `sample.parquet` (and from manifests `manifests/`), and the files the writers produce. | |
| **sample** | The pages a run reads when it is given a sample rule (`--sample N`, `--sample-per-item K`, `--sample-items M`, `--sample-seed S`; `linecaster.data.sample`): chosen from the ids of the input's listing before any image is read, by item rank and page rank, cut after M items, K pages per item and N pages. The same input and options give the same sample whatever the tasks; it goes to `OUT/sample.parquet` and the run record. | not the trace sample; not a preset's `sampling` (decoding settings) |
| **item rank** | An item's place in the sample order (1-based): the items with pages ordered by `H(f"{seed}\t{item_id}")`, ties by id; `H` is the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 as an unsigned big-endian integer. | |
| **page rank** | A page's place within its item in the sample order (1-based): ordered by `H(f"{seed}\t{item_id}\t{page_id}")`, ties by id. | not the page's sequence |
| **run record** | `OUT/run.yaml`: the pipeline as run (every block's parameters, `to_dict()`), the recipe, the command line, the executor and the software, with `pipeline_sha256` (the hash of the functional parameters). | |
| **resource** | A remote file of an item or of one of its pages (a catalogue record, an API's item JSON, a manifest, OCR, an image), with a kind (`marcxml`, `item-json`, ...): fetched as served by `ResourceReader` and kept as a raw copy, `<kind>/<item>/<name>.<ext>`, with a fetch record. | not a datatrove `Media` |
| **HTTP policy**, **host entry** | How a run's requests go out, from one YAML file (`--http-policy`, `linecaster.net.policy`, [http](http.md#the-http-policy)), in three levels: settings for every request at its root (rate limits, retries, deadline, User-Agent, what blocks and what stops the run, `max_pause`), the proxy path's own section (`proxies:`: the list, proxies per worker, how long a blocked or broken proxy is left out), and a host entry under `hosts:` for each host that differs, whose fields replace the root's. The run's own options go between the root and the host entries; each host's settings get their own fetcher. | not several policies |
| **broker** | A shared folder (any `DataFolder`: local, S3, ...) through which workers across tasks, runs and machines agree on who uses which shared resource and what is unavailable until when, with leases and marks (`linecaster.broker`, `--broker`, default `OUT/logs/broker`; [broker](broker.md)). Proxies are its first kind of resource. | not a message broker (no server, no queue) |
| **lease** | A worker's claim on one resource in the broker (`<kind>/<id>/leases/`): it holds the resource while it renews the lease within the lease time (180 s); one worker holds a resource at a time, and a crashed worker's leases expire on their own. | not a lock with a server |
| **mark** | A note in the broker that something holds for a resource in a scope until a time (`<kind>/<id>/marks/<scope>/`), written once and never changed, deleted by whoever sees it expired (past its `keep`, if it has one: kept readable that long after its end, for a proxy's doubling): a proxy's block at a host (scope the host), a broken proxy (scope `*`). | |
| **worker identity**, **worker slot** | Who holds leases in the broker: a datatrove worker as a slot of its machine (`<machine>-<n>`), not a process. A process claims a free slot of its machine at its first use (its search starting at its executor's worker index, so processes started together do not race) and hands it over when it ends; the next process in the slot is the same worker and goes on with its leases (on Ray every task is a new process). | not a process, not a task |
| **proxies per worker** | How many proxies of a list a worker holds at a time (`per_worker` in an HTTP policy's `proxies:` section, per host or at the root, `linecaster.net.proxies`): by default `share`, a fair share of the proxies not blocked (the free ones divided by the live workers), rebalanced as workers come and go; `1`, one, swapped for a free one when it is blocked; or up to N, claimed one by one. The run's default worker count follows it (sharing them, one worker per available proxy up to one per CPU; with `1` or N one per available proxy, divided by N; at most 64 with OUT on object storage). | not proxies per task |
| **block (HTTP)** | A host turning an IP away: a response in the host's `block_on` (429 by default; with `html` there, an HTML page where another format was expected), whether through a proxy or direct, since the server only sees an IP ([http](http.md#blocks)). Through proxies the proxy is left out for that host (a mark in the broker, until `Retry-After`, else 60 s doubling up to `block_ttl`) and the request goes on through another; direct the worker's requests to the host pause. A block is never an attempt. | not a block of a pipeline, not a failed attempt |
| **broken proxy** | A proxy that failed attempts itself (a proxy error, no connection to it) `broken_after` times in a row (3 by default): left out for every host (a mark with scope `*`), first for `broken_ttl` (300 s), doubling, at most `block_ttl`. A slow server's timeout does not count. | not a blocked proxy (that is the host's refusal) |
| **pause** | A time in which a fetcher (one per worker and host settings) sends no request to a host, or with the breaker none at all, and its requests wait instead of failing. Three things start one: a block on a direct connection, for that host, until the response's `Retry-After` has passed, else 60 s doubling while the blocks repeat, after which the request that got it is tried again (`linecaster.net.http.Pause`); the breaker during an outage; and, with a proxy list, no proxy usable for the host (every one the worker holds blocked there, none free to claim) until a block ends or another worker gives one back. The blocks' pauses and the waits for a proxy count toward the host's `max_pause` since its last successful response, and beyond it the run stops ([http](http.md#max_pause)). Other hosts' requests and other workers' fetchers go on. | not a stop of the run |
| **unexpected HTML** | A successful response (2xx) with an HTML page where an image, XML, JSON or a manifest was expected (an error page served with 200, a soft 404, a login page after a redirect): by default a failed attempt, retried and traced `200-html` (`linecaster.net.http.UnexpectedHTML`); a block or a stop where the host's policy has `html` in `block_on` or `stop_on`. | not an error status with an HTML body (a 503 page is a 503) |
| **breaker** | A fetcher's guard against an outage (`linecaster.net.http.Breaker`): when most recent attempts got a server error it pauses the fetcher's requests, sends a probe now and then, and ends the pause with the first answer that is not a server error. | not the pause after a block |
| **reject** | A page that failed a check or a step, written to `rejects/` with the reason; it stays in the page records with its errors. | |
| **warm-up** | What a block loads before its first unit (`warm_up()`): an engine, a server, a client's secrets. Timed as its own stat. | |
| **error budget** | The share of a task's pages a block may fail on before the task fails (`--max-page-errors`, default 1 % of at least 100 pages). | |
| **functional parameter**, **operational parameter** | A block parameter that can change what a run writes (functional), or only where things are and how the work runs (operational: folders, ports, endpoints, windows, worker counts). `pipeline_sha256` covers the functional ones. | |
| **describe mode** | Building a pipeline shape's blocks in the current process without its engines, for its description and hash (`linecaster.runtime.run.describe`). | not `--dry-run`, which runs in the script's environment |
| **secret reference** | `EnvVar("NAME")`: a credential named by its environment variable, read in the task, never stored in a pipeline or a record. | |
| **trace**, **span** | OpenTelemetry's terms: a trace is one page's (or one task's) path through a run, made of spans, one per operation, with times and attributes. | not telemetry |
| **trace sample** | The pages that are traced: a fixed share chosen by page id (`--trace-sample`), plus every page that failed. | not the sample a run reads |
| **trace context** | A page's W3C `traceparent` (`doc.metadata["trace"]`), given at the reader's boundary: the page's spans are its children, and a served block sends it with the page's request. | not "the current span" |
| **task span** | A span of the task's own work, traced for every task: the task, a block's warm-up, a server start, a reader's file, a writer's flush. | |
| **gap** | The time a block had no page in it between its first page and its last: it waited for its input (`linecaster traces`). | |

## Parts

What contracts name besides the parts presets produce (`PRODUCES` in `linecaster.catalog.schema`: `regions`,
`reading_order`, `lines`, `baselines`, `text`, `words`, ...); `PARTS` holds them all.

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | The page image's bytes, as the reader brought them (page-level). |
| `metadata` | The page record's own fields: ids, sequence, the image's record, the metadata (page-level). |
| `transcription_file` | A library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a file's bytes (a document media: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text; page-level); the `TranscriptionConverter` reads it into a transcription. |
| `line_regions` | Lines assigned to the layout regions and ordered within them (the `LineAssigner`). |
| `hierarchy` | Heading levels, headline splits and drop capitals (the `Typographer`). |
| `nfc` | The as-written layer in one Unicode normalization form (the `UnicodeNormalizer`). |
| `paragraphs` | The running text recomposed from the rows, with its decisions (the `Recomposer`). |
| `normalized` | The normalized texts of lines and paragraphs (the `CharacterNormalizer`). |
| `document` | The DoclingDocument of a page (the `Composer`) or of an item (`Composer(unit="item")`). |

## The catalog

| Term | Meaning | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **catalog** | linecaster's register of models, engines, presets and recipes, in `src/linecaster/catalog/data/`. | not a data repository: it holds no measurements |
| **catalog entry** | One registered thing: a model, a preset or a recipe; a YAML file, with a Markdown sidecar for its prose. | not a "component", not a "document" |
| **step** | A catalog step: what an engine does, e.g. `layout`, `lines`, `recognition`, `tables`, `formulas`, `image`, `normalization`, `typography`, `recomposition`, `composition`. A preset belongs to one step. | not a block |
| **engine** | Code with a versioned id (`kraken.recognition.v1`, `recomposition.unicode.v1`) that implements one step: a class with `Options`, capabilities, `load()` and a call per unit. Built-in engines live in the core; engine packages (`linecaster-kraken`, ...) add more. | not saturate's `Engine` class (its server launcher) |
| **strategy** | An engine of a rule-based step (normalization, typography, recomposition, composition, image). A strategy declares the scripts it covers. | |
| **script** | A writing system, named by its ISO 15924 code (`Latn`, `Hebr`, `Arab`): Unicode's `Script` property. A by-script engine routes each decision to the strategy for the script around it; `*` stands for every script. | not a pipeline script |
| **model** | An upstream artifact with weights (or learned data such as hyphenation patterns), pinned by revision, with its upstream card copied verbatim. | not an engine, not a preset, not a VLM adapter |
| **preset** | A named configuration of one engine for one step: engine id, options, capabilities, and the model it loads if any. Referred to as `id@edition`. | |
| **page preset** | A preset whose unit is `page`: one model reads the whole page (a VLM, or a page engine). `launch.py` can run one directly. | not "a model" |
| **page engine** | An engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: it reads the whole page and returns its transcription, in the pipeline's process or behind a server (`indra.recognition.v1`, `surya.recognition.v1`, and the clients of a vendor's service, `falcon.recognition.v1`, `oxr.recognition.v1`). `PageRecognizer` runs it. | not a chat preset (`chat.v1`) |
| **recipe** | A tested combination: a pipeline id, a preset edition per slot, and options. | |
| **slot** | A place in a pipeline script that a preset fills; its name is the step's (`--layout`, `--lines`, `--recognition`, ...). | |
| **repair pass** | A second request for a page whose VLM completion stopped at `max_tokens` (`finish_reason` `length`): the same request with a larger cap (`repair_max_tokens`) and the repair temperature, sent once; the page keeps the second completion where it finished, else the first. Each request of a page is a **pass**, recorded in the transcription's `extra["passes"]`; `extra["kept"]` says which one it holds. | not a retry of a failed request |
| **adapter** | The code that talks to one VLM family over the OpenAI-compatible API: its request, its prompt handling, its parsing (`linecaster.adapters`). | not an engine package |
| **evidence** | A measurement of a preset or recipe edition with its source (own run, model card, vendor benchmark), as an evidence record (`linecaster.evidence/1`), kept by an evaluation in its own repository. | not a catalog entry |
| **version** | Upstream's name for a release of a model (`v6`, `3.5`). | not an edition |
| **revision** | The exact upstream commit a model is pinned to. | |
| **edition** | linecaster's release number of a preset or recipe: `kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1`. A released edition never changes; its hash covers its YAML. | not a version |
| **code id** | The versioned id of an engine or a pipeline: `<name>.v<n>`. An option added later keeps the id if its default keeps the old behavior. | |
| **schema id** | The format of a YAML file: `linecaster.preset/1`. | |
| **lock** | `catalog.lock`: the hash of every released edition, and the expanded pipeline of every recipe edition. | |

## Pages, items and text

| Term | Meaning | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **item** | Any multi-page unit: a book, an issue, a manuscript, a file. Key `item_id`. | not "book" in generic code, flags or docs |
| **page** | One page of an item, with its image and its named transcriptions. `page_id` is `<item_id>_<sequence:04d>` unless the source has stable ids of its own. | not the step `page` (there is none) |
| **page record** | A page with its image reference, its transcriptions and its metadata (`Page`): what a block reads and adds to while the page passes, and what is stored in `OUT/pages/` as JSONL or Parquet (everything but the image bytes). | not a "page row" |
| **item record** | An item with its pages in order, as the `Binder` passes it on (`doc.metadata["item"]`, `linecaster.blocks.base.item`); the item-unit `Recomposer`, `CharacterNormalizer` and `Composer` read it, the item writers write from it, the `Splitter` turns it back into pages. | |
| **manifest** | An item's list of its pages and their files, in order: an IIIF Presentation manifest or a METS document (also inside OAI-PMH). | not a BagIt checksum manifest |
| **page image** | The image a page's coordinates refer to (`PageImage`): its URI, format, size, hash. | |
| **working image** | The `working-image` preset of the `ImageConverter`: lossless WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB. | not a role |
| **transcription** | Everything read from a page by one source (`Transcription`): regions, lines, words, paragraphs, the document, the steps that made it, and its source. Named per page: `ocr_new` (linecaster's), `ocr_original` (the library's own), `ground_truth`. | not "OCR" (it also holds HTR and ground truth) |
| **region** | An area of a page with a label (`text`, `title`, `table`, ...) from layout. | |
| **reading order** | The rank in which a page's regions are read (`Region.reading_order`), from the layout model when it learned one (PP-DocLayoutV3), otherwise computed by linecaster. | not the order of `Transcription.lines`, which is the processing order |
| **XY-cut**, **XY-Cut++** | The two ways linecaster computes a reading order for a layout model that has none: XY-cut splits the page recursively at whitespace gaps; XY-Cut++ (Liu et al., 2025) first masks titles, visuals and cross-layout regions, cuts the rest, then matches the masked regions back to their neighbours (`linecaster.data.geometry`, the layout option `reading_order`). | |
| **cross-layout region** | A text region that spans several columns (longer than 1.3 × the median region and overlapping two or more others horizontally), which XY-Cut++ masks before cutting. | not a region label |
| **line** | One printed or written line: its geometry and, once recognized, its text and words. | |
| **row** | The lines of one region that sit side by side at the same height (`Line.row`), as in typesetting; detection often splits one printed line into several lines on the same row. | never a stored record |
| **word** | The finest unit: its text, box and confidence. linecaster has no glyph level. | |
| **paragraph** | Running text recomposed from a region's rows, with the decisions that made it. Added by the `Recomposer`. | |
| **document** | A DoclingDocument: the composed structure of a page or an item. Added by the `Composer`. | not a datatrove `Document` (say "datatrove document"), not a catalog entry |
| **step info** | One entry per step that worked on a transcription (`StepInfo`): step, engine, preset edition, backend, settings, measurements. | |
| **measurements** | Numbers a step records for a page: seconds, tokens, device, `finish_reason`, in a fixed vocabulary. | not trace attributes |
| **text variant** | A named point on the three text dimensions, written per item: `verbatim_txt`, `readable_txt`, `readable_md`. | not a "version" |
| **character fidelity**, **flow**, **scope** | The three text dimensions: as written → normalized (fidelity); as laid out → flowed (flow); full page → body only (scope). Each transform moves one step on one dimension. | not "axes" |
| **composition** | Building a document from regions and paragraphs (the `Composer`). | not "assembly" |
| **recomposition** | Turning lines back into running text: paragraphs, removed division marks, separators, continuation (the `Recomposer`). | not "reflow" (the old name) |
| **binding** | Gathering an item's pages in order into one item (the `Binder`). | |
| **splitting** | Passing an item record's pages on as pages again, with what the item-level steps added (the `Splitter`). | |
| **division mark** | A hyphen the typesetter added where a word was divided at a line end. | not a hyphen that belongs to the word |
| **decision** | One choice a recomposition made at a row end, with its reason from a fixed vocabulary: a division mark removed, a hyphen kept, a paragraph break, a continuation. Recorded on the paragraph. | |

## Tests

| Term | Meaning | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **engine API** | What an engine package may import from linecaster besides the data model: `linecaster.engines.api` (the `Engine` protocol, `Capabilities`, the weight helpers). | not the HTTP routes of `linecaster serve` |
| **fake engine** | A deterministic CPU engine of `linecaster.testing` for tests, one per model step, registered under `fake.<step>.v1` by `register_fakes()` only. | never in a catalog preset |
| **conformance check** | `check_engine` (the engine protocol) or `check_block` (a block's contract against what it does, its `to_dict()`, pickling, `warm_up()` and failed pages), from `linecaster.testing`. | not a parity check |
| **marker** | A pytest marker of linecaster's tests: `gpu`, `network`, `slow`. Tests marked `gpu` or `network` skip where the device or the network is missing. | |
| **CI workflow** | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the core's tests and checks on a CPU, on every push and pull request to main. | not a workflow |

## Docs and changes

| Term | Meaning | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **derivative** | A project built on linecaster: its own pipelines, blocks or engines, and its project-specific code, defaults and names. | not a fork |
| **generated docs** | The files `linecaster docs` writes from code, docstrings and the catalog when the site is built: the catalog's and the blocks' pages, the site's index and changelog, and `llms.txt`. Never edited by hand and not in git. | not the reference docs (`docs/reference/`, hand-written) |
| **block page** | The generated page of one block (`docs/blocks/<family>/<Block>.md`): its contract, backends, catalog step and presets, position, options, behavior and example. | |
| **breaking change** | A change after which code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference that worked before stops working or means something else ([compatibility](compatibility.md)). | |
| **upgrade note** | The entry in `CHANGELOG.md` for a breaking change: what changed, who is affected, what to do. | |

## The print shop

The block names follow the roles of a hot-metal print shop, in the order they work. linecaster makes a new,
digital edition of a printed item:

| Print shop | linecaster | Does |
|---|---|---|
| the linecaster (casts whole lines) | `LineRecognizer` | casts the lines anew, as text |
| typographer | `Typographer` | determines the hierarchy: headings and their levels, initials, what is text at all |
| compositor | `Recomposer`, `Composer` | recomposes the running text; makes up the page or item document |
| binder | `Binder` | binds the pages into the item (the `Splitter` takes them apart again) |

<!-- docs/reference/conventions.md -->

# Conventions

Rules that hold across the repository. Each rule is followed by its reason. Terms are the
[glossary](glossary.md)'s.

## Names

| What | Pattern | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| block | `<Object><RoleNoun>`; readers and writers `<Object><Format>Reader` / `Writer` | `LineRecognizer`, `Typographer`, `Composer`, `Binder`, `ManifestReader`, `PageJsonlWriter` |
| composite block | `<Purpose><RoleNoun>` | `ModularTranscriber` |
| block base classes | `<Kind>Block` | `PageBlock`, `ModelBlock`, `RuleBlock` |
| engine class | `<Provider><Step>Engine` | `KrakenRecognitionEngine`, `UnicodeRecompositionEngine` |
| engine id | `<provider>.<step>.v<n>` | `kraken.recognition.v1`, `recomposition.unicode.v1` |
| VLM adapter | `<Model>Adapter` | `ChandraOCRAdapter` |
| pipeline script | a verb, `<verb>[_<kind>].py` | `harvest.py`, `transcribe_modular.py`, `transcribe_vlm.py`, `transcribe_page.py`, `bind.py` |
| pipeline id | the script's file name, `.v<n>` | `transcribe_modular.v1` |
| slot and its flag | the step's name | `--layout`, `--lines`, `--recognition` |
| catalog step | a noun for the activity | `layout`, `recognition`, `recomposition` |
| transcription names | `ocr_new`, `ocr_original`, `ground_truth`, or `<source>` | |

Reason: one pattern makes names guessable, and role nouns say what a block is in a pipeline. Pipeline scripts are
verbs because they are what one runs.

## Spelling

American English everywhere: code, flags, docs, commit messages (normalize, recognizer, behavior, license, color,
catalog). Upstream text copied verbatim (model cards) keeps its spelling.

Reason: one spelling for everything typed, matching Python and its ecosystem.

## YAML and Markdown

- Data that tools read is YAML; prose for people is Markdown. A catalog entry is `<id>.yaml`, optionally with
  `<id>.md` next to it; tools never read the Markdown. Reason: Markdown renders cleanly, data validates, and diffs
  of the two do not mix.
- Every YAML file names its format twice: a first line `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to
  src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json>` (editors validate and complete) and a field
  `schema: linecaster.<kind>/<n>` (tools check it). Reason: mistakes show while editing, not at run time.
- The schemas are generated from the pydantic models (`model_json_schema()`) into `src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/`
  (shipped with the package; `linecaster catalog schemas` rewrites them), and a test fails when a committed schema
  differs from a fresh one. The pydantic models are the only source of truth. Reason: one definition, used by
  tools and editors alike.
- YAML is YAML 1.2, read with `ruamel.yaml`: `true`/`false` are the only booleans (`NO` stays a string), duplicate
  keys are errors, and tools that write files back keep their comments.
- An edition's hash covers its functional content (what changes behavior: step, engine, options, pins, settings,
  labels, serving), read from the YAML. The Markdown prose and descriptive fields (support, provenance) are not
  part of it, so they can be corrected without a new edition; git keeps their history.

Schemas: `preset`, `recipe`, `model`, `evidence`, `run-record`, `lock`. Stored page records name their format in a
`schema` field of their row (`linecaster.page/2`).

## Docstrings

Google style, checked by `tests/test_docstrings.py` (with `ast`, no extra tool) for every public block, built-in
engine, backend, serializer, `build`, `run_pages`, `runtime.run.main`, public function of `linecaster.catalog` and
public name of `linecaster.engines.api` and `linecaster.testing`:

- **Summary line**: what the block or function does, in the present tense, starting with a verb, one sentence:
  "Recognizes the text of every line with its engine." It may wrap; it ends at the first blank line. The block
  index and the README's block table show it.
- **Body**: the contract in words (what it reads, adds and replaces), edge cases, what it records (step infos,
  stats, errors on the page).
- **`Args:`** names every parameter of the signature (a class documents its constructor's), and no other: one entry
  each, `name: meaning, the effect of the default, constraints.`, continuation lines indented. Several parameters
  may share an entry (`data_folder, paths_file, ...: datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments.`), as datatrove's
  inherited reader and writer arguments do; `**kwargs` is an entry too. A class that keeps its base's constructor
  keeps its base's `Args:`.
- **`Example:`** (indented Python code) is required for `runtime.run.main`, `build()`, the serializers (`to_alto`,
  `from_alto`, ...) and the public functions of `linecaster.catalog`; optional for blocks, whose generated pages show
  it.
- Inline code in double or single backticks; the generated pages render both as code. Engine options are described
  in their `Options` model (`Field(description=...)`), not in a docstring.

Reason: the generated block pages come from the docstrings, so the reference is only as good as they
are, and a test keeps them complete as signatures change.

## Contracts

- Every block declares its unit and what it reads, adds and replaces ([pipelines](pipelines.md)). A part of the
  record is added by one block only, unless a later block declares that it replaces it. Reason: the builder can then
  check a pipeline before it runs and derive its graph.
- Blocks are pure transforms of their unit; only readers and writers know about tasks, ranks and files. Reason:
  the same blocks run on any executor and in `run_pages()`.

## Tests

- Every built-in engine passes `linecaster.testing.check_engine` and every public block `check_block`
  (`tests/testing/test_conformance.py`); an engine package checks its engines the same way in
  `engines/<engine>/tests/`. Reason: the protocol and the contracts hold for every implementation, not only the
  ones a pipeline happens to run.
- A test that needs a CUDA device is marked `gpu`, one that downloads weights or reaches the internet `network`, one
  over about 10 s `slow` (`--strict-markers`). Reason: the default
  run skips what a machine cannot run, and CI runs what a CPU can.
- Tests use the fake engines, the fake chat server and the fake service of `linecaster.testing`, not copies of their
  own. Reason: one fake per step behaves the same in every test.

## Tracing

- Tracing (OpenTelemetry) is always on. Spans per task always; spans per page for a trace sample chosen by page id, plus
  every page that failed. Reason: where a run loses time is only visible per page and across processes.
- A page carries its trace context from the reader on; blocks open spans as children of the page's context, never
  of "the current span". Reason: pages are interleaved in the stream.
- Attributes are identifiers and numbers under `linecaster.*`, never content (text, images). Reason: content
  belongs in the rows, which the page id links to.
- Traces are written to `OUT/traces/` and, when the standard `OTEL_*` variables are set, exported to a backend
  ([tracing](tracing.md)).

## Telemetry

linecaster sends nothing to anyone that the user did not configure. No usage data, no phoning home, not even
opt-in. Reason: libraries and archives run it on their own infrastructure under their own rules.

## Logging

loguru (datatrove's), with `{placeholder}` templates and named values, never formatted strings:
`logger.warning("page {page_id} failed in {block}: {error}", page_id=..., block=..., error=...)` (the values land in
the record's `extra`). JSON lines on Jobs: the pipeline scripts set `LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1` in their Jobs, where the
tasks (`linecaster.runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor`) and `linecaster serve` log with loguru's `serialize=True`
(`linecaster.runtime.logs`). Log records carry `trace_id` and `span_id`. Reason: logs can be filtered and joined to
traces.

## Errors

Library code raises the classes of `linecaster.errors` (`PipelineConfigError`, `CatalogError`, `PageError`,
`ServerError`, all `LinecasterError`), never `SystemExit`; only the command line (`linecaster`, a pipeline script's
`main`) turns them into exit codes, and a test fails on any other exit. Pure functions of the data model, the formats
and the text transforms keep Python's own `ValueError` for a wrong argument. Reason: a derivative that embeds
linecaster can catch what went wrong, and a run's exit code says whether anything was launched.

## Secrets

A credential is never a value in a pipeline: it is an `EnvVar("NAME")` (`linecaster.runtime.secrets`), read in the
task. Reason: datatrove pickles the pipeline for every executor, and the run record lists every block's parameters.

## Changes

`CHANGELOG.md` in the Keep a Changelog format, with upgrade notes first. `NOTES.md` is the log of measurements and
decisions; reference documents (`docs/reference/`) describe what is, without history.

<!-- docs/reference/architecture.md -->

# Architecture

What linecaster is made of and how a run fits together. Terms are the [glossary](glossary.md)'s; contracts, the
builder, failures and the run record are in [pipelines](pipelines.md), models, presets, recipes and engines in the
[catalog](catalog.md), the page record in the [data model](data-model.md).

## What linecaster is

An open, modular text-recognition suite for print and handwriting (OCR and HTR, old and new documents). It
combines layout, line, text, table and formula recognizers with post-processing (dehyphenation, recomposition,
normalization) into reproducible datatrove pipelines that turn page images into text: the text as written, readable
variants next to it, ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR on request. It is a generalist tool: built on protocols (HTTP,
S3/fsspec, OAI-PMH, IIIF), formats (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, Parquet, JSON Lines) and standards (METS/MODS, Unicode),
it depends on no collection, site, institution or project. Everything that produces text from images lives here;
evaluations and project pipelines (derivatives) are built on top of it.

## Packages

| Package | Holds |
|---|---|
| `linecaster.data` | the data model: `Item`, `Page`, `PageImage`, `Transcription`, `Text`, `StepInfo`, the measurements vocabulary |
| `linecaster.formats` | ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR out and in; the DoclingDocument exports |
| `linecaster.text` | the text transforms: Unicode, typography, recomposition, the text variants |
| `linecaster.images` | the working image, plots |
| `linecaster.engines` | the built-in engines: the rule-based steps and the single-region layout |
| `linecaster.blocks` | the blocks by family ([blocks](../blocks/README.md)) |
| `linecaster.backends` | `InProcess`, `Served`, `Chat` |
| `linecaster.adapters` | one adapter per VLM family, `ADAPTERS` |
| `linecaster.serve` | `linecaster serve` |
| `linecaster.net` | http(s) fetching (`linecaster.net.http`), the HTTP policy, the proxy pools ([http](http.md)) |
| `linecaster.broker` | the [broker](broker.md): leases, marks and worker slots in a shared folder; `linecaster broker` |
| `linecaster.runtime` | the builder, the pipelines' command line, executors, the run record, Jobs helpers, secrets, logs |
| `linecaster.pipelines` | the pipeline shapes, one per pipeline script ([pipelines](pipelines.md#pipeline-shapes)) |
| `linecaster.catalog` | the catalog: its entries, schemas, lock, fetching pins, the docs of its entries |
| `linecaster.tracing` | tracing (OpenTelemetry) and `linecaster traces` |
| `linecaster.docs` | `linecaster docs`: the generated pages |
| `linecaster.testing` | test helpers: sample pages, fake engines (`fake.<step>.v1`, the page engine `fake.recognition.page.v1`), a fake chat server, a fake HTTP service, the conformance checks `check_engine` and `check_block`, the pytest markers |

The first five load neither datatrove nor saturate, nor linecaster's blocks or runtime (`tests/test_import_rule.py`),
so derivatives can use the data model and the formats without the pipeline machinery. datatrove and saturate are
required dependencies, datatrove with its `io` and `s3` extras (`s3://` paths work everywhere), and so is httpx
(`http(s)://` through `linecaster.net`); engines, Ray and PDFium are not (engine packages and extras).

## Blocks and backends

A block is a datatrove `PipelineStep` with a contract; a pipeline is a list of blocks run by a datatrove executor.
Each family is a subpackage of `linecaster.blocks` ([blocks](../blocks/README.md) has a page per block).

**Model blocks** (`ModelBlock`: `LayoutDetector`, `LineDetector`, `LineRecognizer`, `TableRecognizer`,
`FormulaRecognizer`, `PageRecognizer`, `RegionRecognizer`) each have a backend:

- `InProcess("pkg:Class", **kwargs)` (or a preset ref) loads the engine in the worker, in `warm_up()` before the
  first page; a loaded engine is never pickled. In-process is always available and is the parity reference.
- `Served(endpoint, model=name)` and `Chat(preset, endpoint)` (a VLM) stream pages through saturate
  (`AdaptiveClient` and `through()`): a window of pages in flight, adapted to the server's queue gauges and 429s;
  results passed on as they finish; secrets as `EnvVar`. The streaming exists once, in `ModelBlock`.

A page that failed a step carries `doc.metadata["errors"]`, passes later model steps at once and goes to
`rejects/`; more failures than the error budget fail the task ([pipelines](pipelines.md#failures)). Library code
raises `linecaster.errors`, never `SystemExit`.

**Rule blocks** (`RuleBlock`: `Typographer`, `Recomposer`, `Composer`, `CharacterNormalizer`; and `ImageConverter`)
run a built-in engine of a rule-based step in the pipeline's process, picked by a preset.

## One page per request

A request carries one page; engines batch only within a page (kraken batches a page's lines). A page's result
depends only on the page, never on what else is in flight, so runs are deterministic whatever the executor, the
number of tasks or the backend.

## Servers

- **`linecaster serve`** hosts engines: stateless (no state between requests), one worker per model (several
  replicas per model were measured at +7–10 % and removed; NOTES.md), each with a bounded queue (`--max-queue`; a
  full queue answers 429 with `Retry-After`). Routes: `POST /v1/linecaster/{step}` (the image and the transcription
  so far in, the transcription with its part added out), `GET /v1/models`, `/health` and vLLM-shaped `/metrics`
  (the gauges saturate reads). Built-in engines are not served: they run in the pipeline's process.
- **VLMs** run behind OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, SGLang, hosted endpoints): `PageRecognizer` and
  `RegionRecognizer` on the `Chat` backend, on `/v1/chat/completions`, served only. `PageRecognizer` also runs a
  **page engine** (an engine whose unit is the page) on the `InProcess` or `Served` backend: a vendor's package in
  the worker (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page
  pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). A VLM is a catalog preset
  (engine `chat.v1`; its data: revision, prompt, sampling, serve block) plus an adapter in
  `linecaster.adapters.ADAPTERS` (its code: the request, the parsing; `chat_model(<preset>)`).
- **Servers inside a task** (one GPU per HF Job): the server blocks `ModelServer` (`linecaster serve`) and
  `ChatModelServer` (vLLM or SGLang) start the server through saturate's `Engine` and go last in the pipeline,
  after the writer: datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. Each
  task starts its own servers. `ModelServer(script=...)` starts a pipeline script's `serve` with
  `uv run --script`. `ServiceServer` starts the **service** a page preset's `serve` block names: `vllm serve` on the
  pinned checkpoint (fetched and checked) for an engine package that attaches to vLLM, or a vendor image's entrypoint
  (with the weights downloaded to the folder it reads first), ready once its health URLs answer; it runs without the
  pipeline's environment, in the image's own. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the image's fixed ports: one service
  per machine.

## Engines

An engine is a class with a versioned id ([catalog](catalog.md#engines)). Engine packages live in
`engines/<engine>/`, each its own package: `linecaster-kraken`, `linecaster-paddlex`, `linecaster-tesseract`, and the
page engines' `linecaster-indra`, `linecaster-surya` and `linecaster-services` (the clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's
services). An
engine class (`<Provider><Step>Engine`) has `engine_id` (the entry point's name in `linecaster.engines`), `step`,
`capabilities` (unit, produces), an `Options` model (its keyword arguments; a preset's `weights` besides), `load()`
and `__call__(image, transcription, **params) -> Transcription` (the page image as an RGB array, or the image file's
bytes for an engine whose `image_input` is `"bytes"`, and the transcription so far, returned with its part added). Engines with weights load exactly the pin (`weights`,
`linecaster.catalog.fetch`). PaddleX's models load from the pinned snapshot (`create_predictor(model_dir=...)`);
`small-models-for-glam/kraken-blla-base` (the BLLA base model of September 2026) is pinned in
`linecaster_kraken.models`, and no engine uses it. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in
linecaster's catalog. They import from linecaster only `linecaster.data` and the engine API
(`linecaster.engines.api`: the `Engine` protocol, `Capabilities`, the weight helpers), have versions of their own
with a range of linecaster releases, and their tests in `engines/<engine>/tests/` ([catalog](catalog.md#engines)).

## Tests

`uv run pytest` runs the core's tests, one after the other; `uv run pytest -n auto` (pytest-xdist, in the `dev`
group) runs them on every core. Tests marked `gpu` or `network` (`linecaster.testing.markers`: `gpu`, `network`,
`slow`; `--strict-markers`) skip where the device or the network is missing. The CI workflow
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, CPU only, no secrets, uv's cache kept between runs) runs `uv sync --locked
--all-extras` (the extras' readers are tested and documented too), `uv run pytest -n auto -m "not gpu and not
network"`, `linecaster catalog verify`, `linecaster docs` and the site's strict build (the generated
pages are not in git, so CI writes them and a broken reference in them fails the build). The docs workflow
(`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) writes them too and publishes the site with mike on the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves
(`https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/`): a release tag `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` as version `<major>.<minor>`,
with `latest` (the site's default) moved to it; nothing else is published. The engines' environments are too large for it
(torch): their tests (`engines/<engine>/tests/`) and the PEP 723 test
scripts (`tests/test_engines_catalog.py`, `tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py`, `tests/test_line_recognizers.py`) run locally. Every built-in engine and every public
block passes the conformance checks of `linecaster.testing` (`check_engine`: the engine protocol; `check_block`:
the contract against what the block does to sample pages, `to_dict()`, pickling, `warm_up()`, failed pages).

An engine package's tests run in an environment that has the engine: `uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py
engines/<engine>/tests`. `tests/test_engines_catalog.py` holds kraken, PaddleX and Tesseract for the catalog's
line-recognizer presets.

## Recipe scripts

A catalog recipe is YAML (`src/linecaster/catalog/data/recipes/<id>.yaml`: its presets, editions and hash). Its
environment and entry point is a uv script of its own, `recipes/<id>.py`: a PEP 723 block with `linecaster[ray]`
and exactly the engine packages its presets need (recipe → presets → engines → packages:
`linecaster.catalog.code.recipe_packages`), its lock, and a body that only calls
`linecaster.runtime.run.recipe(__file__, "<id>")`, which runs the recipe through its pipeline shape with `--recipe`
set. The pipeline scripts depend on no model choice (`pipelines/transcribe_modular.py` has PaddleX and Tesseract);
the recipes bring theirs (`recipes/squiddle.py`: kraken and PaddleX).

The recipe scripts take linecaster and its engine packages from the `main` branch on GitHub, so a script runs from
its URL with no checkout (`uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py
IMAGES OUT`, `hf jobs uv run <URL> ...`) as well as from one (`uv run recipes/squiddle.py`, `uv run launch.py
squiddle`). A run from the URL resolves the header afresh; a run from a checkout uses the script's lock, whose
linecaster commit moves when it is relocked. Their HF Jobs need no `--commit`: `jobs.dependencies` installs
linecaster from `main` with the lock's versions as constraints. With `--endpoint` the served engines need not be
installed in the client's environment. To preview the site from a checkout: `uv run linecaster docs`, then `uv run --group docs
mkdocs serve`.

## Pipeline scripts

There are no environment folders: a pipeline is a self-contained uv script in `pipelines/` (a PEP 723 block, a
`<script>.py.lock` next to it, `uv run <script>`) that runs one pipeline shape with slots, one script per shape,
never one per machine. The shape is library code, `linecaster.pipelines.<name>` (its options, engines, blocks,
pipeline id and slots), so a derivative's script can run it in its own environment with its own defaults
([pipelines](pipelines.md#pipeline-shapes)):

| Script | Pipeline id | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `harvest.py` | `harvest.v1` | downloads page images (and a library's OCR, manifests) once into item folders, plus page records |
| `transcribe_modular.py` | `transcribe_modular.v1` | lines and a recognizer, optionally layout, tables, formulas, then post-processing; every step a preset the user picks; PaddleX and Tesseract, no kraken |
| `transcribe_vlm.py` | `transcribe_vlm.v1` | a VLM per page or per layout region |
| `transcribe_page.py` | `transcribe_page.v1` | a page engine per page, with the service its preset names |
| `bind.py` | `bind.v1` | item texts and item documents from page records |

`linecaster.runtime.run.main` gives every pipeline the same command line: `--on local|ray|hf-jobs`, `--backend
in-process|served`, `--endpoint` (a running server), `serve` (`linecaster serve` with the script's models), `ray`
(Ray's CLI from the script's environment). Slots have no default presets: every slot is picked, or a recipe fills
them (`--recipe`); `launch.py` runs a recipe or a page preset by name ([catalog](catalog.md#pipelines-recipes-and-launchpy)).
Each script's page in the [catalog's docs](../catalog/README.md) lists its slots and options.

Script environments: the repository is not a uv workspace (engine pins conflict). A script lists what it needs
itself: linecaster with the extra every pipeline uses (`ray` for `--on ray` and `ray start`) and its engine
packages; `s3://` paths need no extra (the core
installs datatrove's `s3` extra, s3fs). A source is
declared by the package that needs it, and `uv lock` applies the sources of path and git dependencies too:
the kraken fork by `linecaster-kraken`, and `stubs/opencv-contrib-python` (the
headless build of the version PaddleX pins; one cv2) by `linecaster-paddlex`. `tests/test_scripts.py` checks
sources, locks and wheels for both machines (uv's `required-environments` does not work in scripts).

torch is never a dependency of the core. Only `linecaster-kraken` pins it (`torch==2.14.0`: kraken's upper bound is
`<=2.14`, and the PyPI 2.14 wheels are the CUDA 13 build on Linux, aarch64 and x86_64), and only environments with
`linecaster-kraken` are bound by that pin; the others take what their own dependencies allow. Each lock's torch is
fixed in `tests/test_scripts.py` (`TORCH`), so it changes only on purpose:

| Environment | torch | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_engines_catalog.py` | 2.14.0 | `linecaster-kraken`'s pin |
| `pipelines/transcribe_page.py`, `tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py` | 2.14.0 | surya-ocr's (`>=2.7,<3`), not pinned: the version it was locked at |
| `tools/cuda_probe.py` | 2.14.0 | its own pin: it probes the CUDA build of `linecaster-kraken`'s torch on a Jobs host |
| `pipelines/transcribe_modular.py`, `transcribe_vlm.py`, `harvest.py`, `bind.py`, `launch.py`, `tests/test_line_recognizers.py`, linecaster's own (`uv.lock`) | none | no engine there needs it |

## Executors and Jobs

| `--on` | Executor |
|---|---|
| `local` | datatrove's `LocalPipelineExecutor` |
| `ray` | `RayGPUExecutor` for stages with servers and single-stage pipelines with engines (one task per GPU), `RayExecutor` (datatrove's `RayPipelineExecutor`) otherwise, on CPUs (an item stage, a harvest; extra `[ray]`); both stop the run at an error that is not the pages', fail a launch that left tasks unfinished, and check first that a live node can run a task |
| `hf-jobs` | `JobsExecutor`: datatrove's `JobsPipelineExecutor` with JSON-lines logs; `GPUJobsExecutor` for multi-GPU flavors |

datatrove's `JobsPipelineExecutor` is experimental and dill-pickles the pipeline, so the launching machine and the
Jobs run the same Python minor version (3.12). `uv run` outside a project drops `[tool.uv.sources]`:
`linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script)` spells out a pipeline's dependencies and sources as URLs, the
installed packages' own sources from the script's lock (the commit must be pushed), and pins every other package at
the lock's version; each Job runs a uv script that carries the pins and the script's overrides, which `uv run --with`
would ignore ([pipelines](pipelines.md#hf-jobs-helpers)).

Workers that share something beyond their tasks (a proxy list, whose proxies each worker may use only while no other
does) agree through the [broker](broker.md), a folder any executor's workers can reach, on any storage datatrove
supports: leases say who holds what, marks what is unavailable until when, and a worker is a slot of its machine that
outlives the processes (on Ray every task is one) that take it over.

## The run layout

One job is one pipeline for one batch on one executor; resume is datatrove's, per task, so tasks stay small. A
pipeline reads the previous folder and writes complete page records with one more part filled in:

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `originals/` | the delivered images and files; never modified |
| `OUT/pages/` | page records (`PageJsonlWriter`, `PageParquetWriter`), bucketed by item id: a whole item in one file, so no joins |
| `OUT/rejects/` | every page that carries errors (`RejectWriter`, put before the first writer by the builder): key, field, error, raw value |
| `OUT/logs/` | datatrove's completion markers, logs and stats; `OUT/logs/broker/`, the [broker](broker.md) by default |
| `OUT/traces/` | the traces ([tracing](tracing.md)) |
| `OUT/run.yaml` | the run record ([pipelines](pipelines.md#the-run-record)) |
| `OUT/sample.parquet` | the sample a run read, one row per page in sample order ([pipelines](pipelines.md#samples)) |
| `OUT/manifests/` | the manifests a sample read (with `sample.jsonl`), or a harvest saved |

`PageRecordReader` reads page records of linecaster's writers, fetching images again by URI (`uri_map` for local
copies). Checks like `PageValidator` record on the page why it failed.

**Readers** follow datatrove's conventions (`BaseDiskReader`: `data_folder`, `paths_file`, `glob_pattern`,
`limit`/`skip` per task; files distributed over tasks in turn, Parquet tables by rows in equal shards,
`linecaster.blocks.readers.tables`, so a table needs no splitting): `ImageFolderReader` (image files),
`ImageParquetReader` (an image column: bytes, an HF image struct or a path), `ManifestReader` (IIIF or METS, parsed
by `linecaster.formats.manifests`, its files fetched through `linecaster.net.http`; a manifest,
or a row of a Parquet item table, is an entry, so an item stays in one task; a IIIF Collection entry is its
manifests, one level; `existing_ocr` fetches a library's OCR as a document media, which a `TranscriptionConverter`
reads as `ocr_original`, the builder adding one when missing), `PdfReader` (PDF files as items, pages rendered with
pypdfium2, extra `[pypdfium2]`) and `PageRecordReader`. Readers that fetch over http(s) request ahead in a window
that grows while no request waits for the rate limits (`linecaster.net.http.prefetched`), through one fetcher per
process and configuration, so the limits hold across a worker's tasks; `ImageParquetReader` and `ManifestReader`
suggest a task count from their input (`auto_tasks`), which a pipeline without engines runs with
([pipelines](pipelines.md#tasks-workers-and-rate-limits)).

**The workflow** is harvest → transcribe → bind: `pipelines/harvest.py` downloads images (and OCR, manifests) once
into item folders plus page records, the transcribe pipelines read those with `--pages`, `pipelines/bind.py` makes
item texts and documents. An item's pages can land in different tasks; item-level steps are a second stage over item
shards (`--item-shards N` writes `OUT/pages/<shard>/<rank>`, `pipelines/bind.py` reads whole shards), as datatrove's
own multi-stage pipelines read per-bucket folders ([pipelines](pipelines.md#the-item-stage)).

<!-- docs/reference/pipelines.md -->

# Pipelines: contracts and the builder

A pipeline is a list of blocks (datatrove `PipelineStep`s) and composites. Before it runs, the builder
(`linecaster.runtime.builder`) checks the blocks' contracts, expands the composites, and cuts the pipeline into
stages. Every pipeline script goes through it (`linecaster.runtime.run`). Terms are the [glossary](glossary.md)'s.

## Contracts

Every block returns its contract from `contract()` (`linecaster.blocks.base.contract`):

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Part:
    name: str                  # a name of PARTS, or "*" (every part)
    transcription: str | None  # ocr_new, ocr_original, ...; None: page-level (image, metadata, transcription_file)
                               # or the item record's

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Contract:
    unit: str                  # "page", "item" (what the input stream carries) or "any" (servers)
    unit_out: str | None       # set when the block changes the stream's unit (binder: page -> item, splitter: back)
    reads: frozenset[Part]
    adds: frozenset[Part]
    replaces: frozenset[Part]
    removes: frozenset[Part]   # parts the block does not pass on (gone for every later block)
    role: str                  # reader, writer, server, model, transform, binder, splitter, validator, composite
```

- **The vocabulary** is `PARTS` in `linecaster.catalog.schema`: `image`, `metadata` and `transcription_file` (a
  library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a document media) (page-level), what presets produce (`PRODUCES`: `regions`, `reading_order`, `lines`, `baselines`, `text`, `words`, `word_confidences`,
  `line_confidences`, `tables`, `formulas`, `markdown`, `html`, `doctags`, `layout_json`, `latex`), and
  `line_regions`, `hierarchy`, `nfc`, `document`. A part is written `transcription:name` (`ocr_new:lines`);
  `ocr_original:*` is every part of a transcription.
- **Simple blocks** declare class attributes (`unit`, `role`, `parts_read`, `parts_added`, `parts_replaced`,
  `parts_removed`) that
  the default `contract()` of `Contracted` reads; page-level names stay page-level, the others belong to the
  block's `transcription`. Blocks whose parts depend on their options compute `contract()`.
- **Model blocks** read the page image (recognition also `lines`, tables and formulas `regions`) and add their
  preset's `capabilities.produces`: the preset of the `InProcess` backend (`preset`), of the `Served` backend
  (`preset`, set by `runtime.run.engines`) or of the `Chat` backend; without a preset the engine class's
  `capabilities` (read from its source in the repository, else from the class); without either the step's default.
  The chat recognizers add `text` too, `RegionRecognizer` also `lines` (and replaces `lines` and `text`: the
  transcription's earlier lines are replaced).
- **Readers** add `image` and `metadata`; `ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True)` also `transcription_file`, which the
  `TranscriptionConverter` reads (adding `ocr_original:*`);
  `PageRecordReader` what `provides=` declares (`["ocr_new:lines", ...]`), or anything (`*`, reads after it are
  not checked) when it declares nothing. With `fetch_images=False` it brings no `image`.
- **Writers** read what they write and add nothing (`ImageFilesWriter` replaces `metadata`: the image's URI then
  names its copy; `PageFileWriter`: `lines` for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, `text` for
  md and txt, `document` for HTML, DocLang and JSON, `image` for plots). **Servers** have role `server` and unit
  `any`.
- **The `Binder`** changes the unit from pages to items, the **`Splitter`** back: an item record holds its page
  records, so what the pages carried stays available across either (the checks carry the parts over), apart from
  the page image's bytes (`image`: an item record has none) at the binder and the item's `document` at the splitter.
- **Item-unit blocks** (`Recomposer(unit="item")`, `CharacterNormalizer(unit="item")`, `Composer(unit="item")`)
  read item records: one datatrove document per item, `doc.metadata["item"]` holding the item id and its page records
  in order (`linecaster.blocks.base.item`); they read and add the parts of the pages' transcriptions, the item
  `Composer` adds the item's `document` next to the record. **Item writers**: `ItemTextWriter` reads `lines` for
  `verbatim_txt` and `paragraphs` and `normalized` for the readable variants, `ItemDocumentWriter` the `document`.
  `RecipeStamper` has unit `any`: before an item writer it stamps the pages of each item record.
- A step without a contract (a plain datatrove step) passes pages and touches no part.

| Block | Reads | Adds | Replaces, removes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LineAssigner` | `lines`, `regions` | `line_regions` | `regions`, `reading_order`, `lines` |
| `UnicodeNormalizer` | `text` | `nfc` | `text` |
| `CharacterNormalizer` | `text` | `normalized` | |
| `Typographer` | `regions`, `lines` | `hierarchy` | `regions`, `lines` |
| `Recomposer` | `regions`, `lines` | `paragraphs` | `paragraphs` (made anew where they exist) |
| `Composer` | `regions`, `lines` (and `paragraphs` when there are) | `document` | |
| `ImageFetcher` | `metadata` | | `image` |
| `ImageConverter` | `metadata` | | `metadata` (with `keep_bytes` also `image`; without it removes `image`) |
| `TranscriptionConverter` | `metadata`, `transcription_file` (with `source="media"`) | `<transcription>:*` | |
| `RecipeStamper` | | | |

## Block shapes

- **Per-unit transform** (`shape = "unit"`): `process_page(doc, page) -> page | None`; `PageBlock` owns the loop
  and the stats. In-process model blocks have this shape.
- **Stream transform** (`shape = "stream"`): overrides `run(data)` and yields each page when it is done, possibly
  out of order (served model blocks, `PageRecognizer`, `RegionRecognizer`). It reports what happens to each page
  inside it with `notify(doc, event)`: `prepare` when a request is built, `done` when its result came back. The
  served model blocks share one streaming loop (`ModelBlock`): a block names its requests (`_rows`: one per page, one
  per region for `RegionRecognizer`), builds and parses each (`_request`, `_parse`) and says which pages a finished
  one completes (`_done`).
- Only readers and writers see `rank`, `world_size` and files (a test walks every block class, with no exceptions):
  a block that rejects a page records why on the page, and the `RejectWriter` names the task's file.

## Backends

A model block's backend (`linecaster.backends`) says where its engine runs:

- `InProcess("pkg:Class", **options)` (or `InProcess.from_preset(ref)`; a model block given a preset ref,
  `LayoutDetector("single-region@1")`, builds one): the engine loads in the worker;
- `Served(endpoint, model=name, ...)`: `linecaster serve` (or a server speaking its routes) hosts it, reached through
  saturate on `/v1/linecaster/{step}`;
- `Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None,
  headers=None, prefer="page")`: a chat preset's VLM behind an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, a hosted
  endpoint) on `/v1/chat/completions`; `preset` is a preset ref, a model's Hugging Face id (its preset with unit
  `prefer`) or a configured adapter (`chat_model`); without an endpoint, the task's `ChatModelServer` on port 8000.
  `PageRecognizer(backend)` and `RegionRecognizer(backend, labels=..., pad=None)` (`pad`: the adapter's `region_pad`, else 8) take it (or a chat preset's ref).
  `Chat(..., overrides={...})` sets the chat engine's options over the preset's settings (`max_tokens`, `temperature`,
  `top_p`, `repair_max_tokens`, `repair_temperature`; `--set recognition.<option>=<value>` in
  `pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py`); the ones that differ from the preset's are recorded with the adapter
  (`overrides`) and count in `pipeline_sha256`. With `repair_max_tokens` set, `PageRecognizer` runs the
  [repair pass](glossary.md): a page whose completion stopped at `max_tokens` waits while its second request goes
  into the same window, and leaves the block with both recorded; `PageRecognizer(..., repair_only=True)` sends only
  the repair requests, for page records read with `PageRecordReader` (`--pages ... --repair-only`). The streaming
  loop of `ModelBlock` offers this to every served block: a finished request may ask for a second one
  (`_second_request`), whose response comes back with it (`_second_done`).
  `PageRecognizer` also takes a page engine's `InProcess` or `Served` backend (or its preset's ref): a stream
